source.title: Natural selective attention: orienting and emotion

confidence_rationale: Standard, well-cited review of the Sokolov-lineage human psychophysiological orienting response literature, giving the classical multi-second time course of the ORIENTING EPISODE itself (Q1b's cross-check quantity) rather than the post-decision persistence question (Q1) directly. Confidence held at moderate because it is a review synthesizing others' data rather than a primary quantitative source, and because it characterizes autonomic/attentional orienting components, not a behavioral action-selection bias.
failure_signatures: If SD-099's post-orienting bias window were meant to be much SHORTER than the orienting episode it follows, that would be a novel and unsupported claim -- every human psychophysiological component of the orienting response reviewed here (cardiac deceleration, electrodermal response, late positive potential) unfolds and resolves on a multi-second timescale, not a sub-200ms one.

mapping.source_claim_statement: The orienting response is not a single reflex but a cascade of dissociable components -- an early perceptual/cardiac-deceleration component, later electrodermal (action-readiness) and cortical (late positive potential, significance-detection) components -- that unfold and habituate at different rates across the seconds following an eliciting stimulus, organized by underlying defensive and appetitive motivational systems rather than being a unitary all-or-none event.
mapping.ree_translation: This is Q1b's cross-check quantity: the duration of the orienting EPISODE itself, against which SD-099's post-decision bias persistence should be compared. Classical psychophysiology places the OR's own components on a multi-second time course (cardiac deceleration typically peaking several seconds post-onset, later components later still), which is the same order of magnitude as the Shang 2018 and Vale 2017 entries' measured post-decision freezing durations in this directory, not two orders of magnitude smaller. This is the source SD-099's own functional_restatement cites as 'the Sokolov orienting-reflex shape' -- this entry grounds that citation with the actual quantitative time course rather than leaving it as an unstated assumption.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Human, not rodent; autonomic/attentional/electrocortical components of orienting (heart rate, skin conductance, EEG), not a behavioral action-selection bias or an approach/withdraw decision. This is a review's synthesis of a large prior literature, not a single new measurement, so the specific numbers it reports should be read as a well-established consensus range rather than a single-study point estimate. It does not itself address SD-099's approach/withdraw/resume decision at all -- it grounds only the 'how long does orienting itself take' half of the comparison (Q1b), not the post-decision persistence half (Q1).

confidence_components.notes: Source quality solid (established Psychophysiology review, well-cited, synthesizes a mature literature). Mapping fidelity moderate -- directly answers Q1b's cross-check quantity (orienting-episode duration) but says nothing about Q1's post-decision persistence question, and is human autonomic physiology rather than rodent defensive-behavior or REE's abstract decision architecture. Transfer risk moderate: human-to-agent and physiology-to-behavior gaps, offset by this being the specific theoretical lineage (Sokolov) SD-099's own design doc already invokes.
